the anisotropy of the nuclear resonance fluorescence yield of 1,37 MeV gamma rays emitted from Mg24 recoils was determined in a backscattering experiment.
the NRF yield of 1,37 MeV quanta emitted from Mg24 recoils in single crystals of Na or NaCl depends on the direction of quantas relative to orientation of the crystals.
the NRF yield of the gamma radiation emitted from recoils of the Mg24 is anisotropic.

the NRF yield of the Mg24 recoils in NaCl is reduced by 10% and in Na by 20% relative to the yield in vacuum.

the anisotropic absorption cross section of the Mg24 nuclei in single crystals of NaCl and Na is caused by the anisotropic stopping power of the nuclei in the crystals.
